concepts.name: Axes & planes
concepts.def_ours: Cranial–caudal, dorsal–ventral and left–right, shown on a rotating disc.

concepts.name: Days, weeks & Carnegie stages
concepts.def_ours: How embryos are dated; fertilization age vs gestational (LMP) age; the stage ruler.
concepts.misconception: Gestational age and fertilization age are the same number.

concepts.name: Scale
concepts.def_ours: A zoom ruler from 0.1 mm to 30 cm, shown on every 3D view.

concepts.name: Colour key
concepts.def_ours: Fixed germ-layer colours with patterns and labels, safe for colour-blind viewers.

concepts.name: Reading a section
concepts.def_ours: How a flat slice relates to the 3D shape it cuts through.

concepts.name: How to use the app
concepts.def_ours: Watch it · Try it · Remember deck · Check.

concepts.name: Chromatin and nucleosomes
concepts.def_ours: DNA wound on histone spools; how tightly it is packed decides which genes can be read.

concepts.name: Gene structure: promoter, exons, introns
concepts.def_ours: A gene has a promoter where reading starts, exons that code and introns that are cut out.

concepts.name: Transcription factors
concepts.def_ours: Proteins that bind DNA and switch genes on or off; master regulators of development.

concepts.name: Enhancers
concepts.def_ours: DNA stretches, often far away, that boost a gene's promoter in particular tissues.

concepts.name: Alternative splicing
concepts.def_ours: One gene can make several proteins by joining its exons in different ways.

concepts.name: DNA methylation and imprinting
concepts.def_ours: Chemical tags silence genes without changing the sequence; imprinted genes are read from one parent only.
concepts.misconception: Imprinting changes the DNA sequence.

concepts.name: Induction
concepts.def_ours: One tissue changes the fate of a neighbouring tissue; the responder must be competent to react.
concepts.misconception: Induction is a one-way, one-off signal (most are reciprocal and repeated).

concepts.name: Epithelial–mesenchymal interactions
concepts.def_ours: Organs form from repeated two-way talk between an epithelium and the mesenchyme beneath it.

concepts.name: Paracrine and juxtacrine signalling
concepts.def_ours: Signals that diffuse to nearby cells (paracrine) vs signals passed by direct cell contact (juxtacrine).

concepts.name: Morphogen gradients
concepts.def_ours: A signal whose concentration tells cells where they are, so one source can pattern a whole field.

concepts.name: Sonic hedgehog (SHH) pathway
concepts.def_ours: A key signal for midline, neural tube, limb and gut patterning; its loss causes midline defects.

concepts.name: WNT pathway
concepts.def_ours: Signals that drive growth and polarity, acting through β-catenin.

concepts.name: TGF-β superfamily (BMPs, Nodal)
concepts.def_ours: A large family of growth factors including BMPs and Nodal, used in axis setting and organ shaping.

concepts.name: FGFs and receptor tyrosine kinases
concepts.def_ours: Growth factors that act through receptor kinases; drive limb outgrowth and many inductions.

concepts.name: Notch signalling
concepts.def_ours: A contact signal between neighbouring cells, used to make cells choose different fates.

concepts.name: Retinoic acid
concepts.def_ours: A vitamin A derivative that patterns the head–tail axis; too much is teratogenic.

concepts.name: Primordial germ cells
concepts.def_ours: Germ cells set aside in the epiblast that migrate through the yolk-sac wall and hindgut to the gonads.
concepts.misconception: Germ cells start in the gonad.

concepts.name: Teratomas from germ cells
concepts.def_ours: Stray germ or pluripotent cells can form tumours containing tissues of all three layers.

concepts.name: Mitosis
concepts.def_ours: One division that makes two identical diploid cells.

concepts.name: Meiosis
concepts.def_ours: Two divisions that halve the chromosome number and shuffle genes by crossing over.
concepts.misconception: Crossing over happens in meiosis II.

concepts.name: Nondisjunction and numerical abnormalities
concepts.def_ours: Chromosomes fail to separate, giving trisomy (21, 18, 13), Klinefelter (47,XXY) or monosomy (Turner); risk rises with maternal age.

concepts.name: Structural chromosome abnormalities
concepts.def_ours: Breaks give translocations, deletions and microdeletions; Prader-Willi vs Angelman (15q) depends on the parent of origin; fragile X is a fragile site.

concepts.name: Mosaicism
concepts.def_ours: Two or more cell lines with different karyotypes in one person, usually from an error after fertilization.

concepts.name: Karyotype and genetic testing
concepts.def_ours: Ways to look at chromosomes and genes: karyotype, FISH, microarray, sequencing.

concepts.name: Oogenesis
concepts.def_ours: Oocytes start meiosis before birth and pause; meiosis I finishes just before ovulation, then it pauses again until fertilization completes meiosis II.
concepts.misconception: Women make new eggs every month.

concepts.name: Follicle maturation
concepts.def_ours: Primordial → primary → secondary (antral) follicle around the oocyte.

concepts.name: Spermatogenesis
concepts.def_ours: From puberty, spermatogonia divide into spermatocytes and spermatids, supported by Sertoli cells.

concepts.name: Spermiogenesis
concepts.def_ours: Shaping a round spermatid into a sperm: acrosome, condensed head, tail.
concepts.misconception: Spermiogenesis is another word for spermatogenesis.

concepts.name: Abnormal gametes
concepts.def_ours: Gametes with extra or missing chromosomes or abnormal shapes; a cause of early loss.

concepts.name: Ovarian cycle and its hormones
concepts.def_ours: Hypothalamus and pituitary (GnRH, FSH, LH) drive follicle growth each cycle.

concepts.name: Ovulation
concepts.def_ours: An LH surge releases the secondary oocyte from the follicle mid-cycle.
concepts.misconception: Ovulation is always on day 14.

concepts.name: Corpus luteum
concepts.def_ours: The emptied follicle makes progesterone; hCG from the embryo keeps it going in pregnancy.

concepts.name: Oocyte transport
concepts.def_ours: Fimbriae sweep the oocyte into the tube; cilia and muscle move it toward the uterus.

concepts.name: Capacitation and acrosome reaction
concepts.def_ours: Sperm are primed in the female tract, then release acrosome enzymes at the zona.

concepts.name: Fertilization
concepts.def_ours: In the ampulla a sperm fuses with the oocyte; the zona reaction blocks others; meiosis II completes.
concepts.misconception: Fertilization happens in the uterus.

concepts.name: Results of fertilization
concepts.def_ours: Diploid number restored, sex decided by the sperm, and cleavage starts.

concepts.name: Contraception and assisted reproduction
concepts.def_ours: How contraception works and how IVF and ICSI help with infertility.

concepts.name: Cleavage and morula
concepts.def_ours: Rapid divisions with no overall growth make smaller blastomeres and a morula by about day 3.
concepts.misconception: The embryo grows during cleavage.

concepts.name: Compaction; inner and outer cell mass
concepts.def_ours: Blastomeres pack tightly and split into an inner cell mass and an outer cell mass.

concepts.name: Blastocyst
concepts.def_ours: A fluid cavity forms; the embryoblast (inner cell mass) sits at one pole inside the trophoblast.

concepts.name: Implantation begins
concepts.def_ours: The blastocyst hatches from the zona and the trophoblast attaches to the uterine lining.

concepts.name: Epiblast and hypoblast
concepts.def_ours: The inner cell mass splits into two layers: epiblast and hypoblast.

concepts.name: Anterior visceral endoderm sets the head end
concepts.def_ours: Hypoblast cells at one edge signal to mark the future cranial end.

concepts.name: Embryonic stem cells
concepts.def_ours: Cells of the inner cell mass can make any tissue; uses and limits in medicine.

concepts.name: Uterus at implantation
concepts.def_ours: The secretory-phase endometrium, its three layers, and where the blastocyst usually implants.

concepts.name: Menstrual cycle phases
concepts.def_ours: Proliferative, secretory and menstrual phases of the uterine lining.

concepts.name: Cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast
concepts.def_ours: The trophoblast splits into an inner cell layer and an outer invasive multinucleated layer.

concepts.name: Bilaminar disc
concepts.def_ours: Epiblast and hypoblast form a flat two-layered disc.

concepts.name: Amniotic cavity
concepts.def_ours: A cavity opens in the epiblast, lined by amnioblasts.

concepts.name: Trophoblastic lacunae
concepts.def_ours: Spaces open in the syncytiotrophoblast.

concepts.name: Primitive yolk sac and exocoelomic membrane
concepts.def_ours: Cells from the hypoblast line the blastocyst cavity, forming the primitive yolk sac.

concepts.name: Uteroplacental circulation begins
concepts.def_ours: The syncytium erodes maternal capillaries so maternal blood flows through the lacunae.

concepts.name: Extraembryonic mesoderm
concepts.def_ours: A loose tissue fills the space around the yolk sac and amnion and splits into two layers.

concepts.name: Decidual reaction
concepts.def_ours: Stromal cells of the endometrium swell with stored nutrients around the implanting embryo.

concepts.name: Primary villi
concepts.def_ours: Cytotrophoblast columns push into the syncytium.

concepts.name: Secondary yolk sac
concepts.def_ours: A smaller definitive yolk sac forms; exocoelomic cysts pinch off.

concepts.name: Chorionic cavity and connecting stalk
concepts.def_ours: The extraembryonic coelom becomes the chorionic cavity; the embryo hangs from the connecting stalk.

concepts.name: Abnormal implantation and ectopic pregnancy
concepts.def_ours: Implantation outside the uterine body, most often the tube; can rupture and bleed.

concepts.name: Hydatidiform mole and hCG
concepts.def_ours: Trophoblast overgrowth without a normal embryo; high hCG; risk of choriocarcinoma.

concepts.name: Prechordal plate
concepts.def_ours: A thickened area at the cranial end that marks the head and signals the forebrain.

concepts.name: Oropharyngeal and cloacal membranes
concepts.def_ours: Places where ectoderm and endoderm touch with no mesoderm: future mouth and future anus.

concepts.name: Gastrulation in one picture
concepts.def_ours: In week 3 the two-layered disc becomes three layers: ectoderm, mesoderm, endoderm.

concepts.name: Primitive streak
concepts.def_ours: A groove on the epiblast with a node and pit at its head; it marks the body axis.
concepts.misconception: The primitive streak is permanent (it shrinks and vanishes).

concepts.name: Cells move in
concepts.def_ours: Epiblast cells leave the surface and pass through the streak to make the new layers.
concepts.misconception: The hypoblast becomes the endoderm (epiblast cells replace it).

concepts.name: Three germ layers from the epiblast
concepts.def_ours: Epiblast makes all three layers: what stays is ectoderm, what moves in is mesoderm and endoderm.
concepts.misconception: Mesoderm comes from the hypoblast.

concepts.name: Notochord
concepts.def_ours: A midline rod formed from cells entering at the node; signals the neural tube and later the disc core.
concepts.misconception: The notochord becomes the vertebral column.

concepts.name: Neurenteric canal
concepts.def_ours: A brief opening that links the amniotic cavity and yolk sac during notochord formation.

concepts.name: Body axes are set
concepts.def_ours: Head–tail, back–belly and left–right axes are fixed before and during gastrulation.

concepts.name: Left–right signals
concepts.def_ours: Cilia at the node move fluid leftward; Nodal and PITX2 become active on the left only.

concepts.name: The node as organizer
concepts.def_ours: Node signals block BMP so the overlying ectoderm becomes neural.

concepts.name: Fate map: three layers → what they become
concepts.def_ours: Ectoderm → skin and nervous system; mesoderm → muscle, bone, blood; endoderm → gut and lung lining.

concepts.name: Streak position decides mesoderm type
concepts.def_ours: Cells entering cranially become paraxial; mid-streak intermediate; caudally lateral plate and extraembryonic.

concepts.name: Growth of the disc
concepts.def_ours: The disc becomes pear-shaped as the head end grows and the streak shortens.

concepts.name: When gastrulation goes wrong
concepts.def_ours: Damage in week 3 can cause caudal dysgenesis (sirenomelia) or midline face and brain defects.

concepts.name: Sacrococcygeal teratoma
concepts.def_ours: A tumour from leftover primitive-streak cells at the base of the spine.

concepts.name: Situs inversus and laterality defects
concepts.def_ours: Organs reversed (situs inversus) or mixed up (heterotaxy) when left–right signals fail.

concepts.name: Secondary and tertiary villi
concepts.def_ours: Mesoderm grows into the villi, then blood vessels form in them.

concepts.name: Cytotrophoblast shell; stem and free villi
concepts.def_ours: Trophoblast spreads to anchor the chorion to the endometrium.

concepts.name: Villi join the embryo's circulation
concepts.def_ours: Vessels in villi connect through the connecting stalk to the heart as it starts to beat.

concepts.name: Embryonic period: weeks 3–8
concepts.def_ours: Embryogenesis proper: every major organ starts forming; the most sensitive time for birth defects.
concepts.misconception: The most dangerous time for teratogens is late pregnancy.

concepts.name: Neural induction and neural plate
concepts.def_ours: Blocking BMP makes midline ectoderm thicken into the neural plate.

concepts.name: Neurulation
concepts.def_ours: Neural folds rise and fuse, starting in the neck region and zipping both ways into a tube.
concepts.misconception: The neural tube closes all at once.

concepts.name: Neuropores close
concepts.def_ours: The cranial neuropore closes around day 25, the caudal around day 28.

concepts.name: Neural crest cells
concepts.def_ours: Cells at the fold edges leave the tube and migrate widely.
concepts.misconception: Neural crest is part of the CNS.

concepts.name: Neural crest derivatives
concepts.def_ours: Sensory and autonomic ganglia, Schwann cells, melanocytes, adrenal medulla, face bones, heart outflow septum.

concepts.name: Ectoderm derivatives and placodes
concepts.def_ours: Epidermis, hair, nails, glands, enamel, anterior pituitary; placodes for ear and lens.

concepts.name: Neural tube defects
concepts.def_ours: Failure to close gives spina bifida or anencephaly; folic acid lowers the risk.

concepts.name: Paraxial, intermediate and lateral plate mesoderm
concepts.def_ours: Mesoderm beside the midline separates into three strips.

concepts.name: Somites
concepts.def_ours: Paraxial mesoderm buds off blocks about three pairs a day; their count dates the embryo.
concepts.misconception: Somites are segments of the neural tube.

concepts.name: Segmentation clock
concepts.def_ours: Oscillating gene activity plus FGF/WNT and retinoic acid gradients set when each somite forms.

concepts.name: Somite differentiation
concepts.def_ours: Sclerotome → skeleton; dermomyotome → muscle (myotome) and dermis (dermatome).
concepts.misconception: The dermatome forms the epidermis.

concepts.name: Intermediate mesoderm
concepts.def_ours: The strip that gives the kidneys and gonads.

concepts.name: Lateral plate mesoderm
concepts.def_ours: Splits into a body-wall (parietal) layer and a gut-wall (visceral) layer around a cavity.

concepts.name: Vasculogenesis and angiogenesis
concepts.def_ours: New vessels from blood islands (vasculogenesis) vs sprouting from existing ones (angiogenesis).
concepts.misconception: The two words mean the same thing.

concepts.name: Sites of blood formation
concepts.def_ours: Yolk sac first, then the aorta region, liver, and finally bone marrow.

concepts.name: Capillary haemangiomas
concepts.def_ours: Common benign vessel overgrowths in infants.

concepts.name: Body folding
concepts.def_ours: Head, tail and side folds turn the flat disc into a tube-shaped body.
concepts.misconception: The whole yolk sac becomes the gut.

concepts.name: Foregut, midgut, hindgut
concepts.def_ours: Folding pinches endoderm into a gut tube; the midgut stays linked to the yolk sac by the vitelline duct.

concepts.name: Endoderm derivatives
concepts.def_ours: Lining of gut, lungs, bladder and glands; liver and pancreas cells; pouch derivatives.

concepts.name: Hox genes pattern the head–tail axis
concepts.def_ours: Hox genes switch on in the same order as their chromosome position, giving each segment its identity.

concepts.name: External appearance in month 2
concepts.def_ours: Big head, face forming, limbs with digits, crown–rump length grows fast.

concepts.name: Estimating embryo age
concepts.def_ours: Somite count in week 4, then crown–rump length and ultrasound.

concepts.name: Body plan after folding
concepts.def_ours: After folding: neural tube above, gut tube below, inside a body-wall tube.

concepts.name: Intraembryonic body cavity
concepts.def_ours: A single cavity forms inside lateral plate mesoderm and later divides.

concepts.name: Somatopleure vs splanchnopleure
concepts.def_ours: Parietal layer + ectoderm make the body wall; visceral layer + endoderm make the gut wall.
concepts.misconception: The somatopleure lines the gut.

concepts.name: Serous membranes and mesenteries
concepts.def_ours: Peritoneum, pleura and pericardium; mesenteries are double layers holding the gut.

concepts.name: Body wall defects
concepts.def_ours: Omphalocele (gut in a sac at the cord), gastroschisis (beside the cord, no sac), ectopia cordis, bladder exstrophy.
concepts.misconception: Omphalocele and gastroschisis are the same defect.

concepts.name: Septum transversum
concepts.def_ours: A thick mesoderm plate between heart and yolk stalk; it gives the liver's connective tissue and the ventral mesentery and is the base the diaphragm forms on.
concepts.misconception: The septum transversum becomes the central tendon.

concepts.name: Separating pleural from pericardial cavities
concepts.def_ours: Pleuropericardial folds close the canals between them, carrying the phrenic nerves.

concepts.name: Diaphragm from four parts
concepts.def_ours: Pleuroperitoneal membranes (central tendon + scaffold) grow over the septum transversum; muscle from C3–C5 somites; oesophageal mesentery gives the crura; nerve C3–C5.
concepts.misconception: The diaphragm forms where it ends up (it starts high in the neck).

concepts.name: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia
concepts.def_ours: A posterolateral (usually left) hole lets gut into the chest and stunts the lung.

concepts.name: Fetal period growth
concepts.def_ours: Months 3–9: length grows most in months 3–5, weight in the last two months.

concepts.name: Growth restriction and prematurity
concepts.def_ours: Low birth weight and growth restriction, their causes and risks.

concepts.name: Time of birth
concepts.def_ours: About 266 days after fertilization, or 280 days (40 weeks) after the last period.
concepts.misconception: Forty weeks is counted from fertilization.

concepts.name: Chorion and fetal membranes
concepts.def_ours: The chorion with its villi and the amnion around the fetus.

concepts.name: Preeclampsia
concepts.def_ours: Maternal high blood pressure and protein loss linked to shallow trophoblast remodelling of spiral arteries.

concepts.name: Chorion frondosum and laeve; deciduae
concepts.def_ours: Villi stay on the side facing the decidua basalis (frondosum) and vanish elsewhere (laeve).

concepts.name: Structure of the placenta
concepts.def_ours: Fetal villi bathe in maternal blood in the intervillous space, divided into cotyledons.
concepts.misconception: Maternal and fetal blood mix in the placenta.

concepts.name: The placental membrane
concepts.def_ours: A thin barrier that passes gases, nutrients, IgG, many drugs and some viruses.
concepts.misconception: The placenta blocks drugs and microbes.

concepts.name: Placenta as an endocrine organ
concepts.def_ours: Makes hCG, progesterone, oestrogens and placental lactogen.

concepts.name: Rh disease and fetal hydrops
concepts.def_ours: Maternal antibodies cross and destroy fetal red cells.

concepts.name: Placenta accreta and previa
concepts.def_ours: Villi invade too deep (accreta/increta/percreta) or implant over the cervix (previa).

concepts.name: Umbilical cord
concepts.def_ours: Two arteries and one vein in jelly, covered by amnion; a single artery can flag other defects.
concepts.misconception: Umbilical arteries carry oxygen-rich blood.

concepts.name: Placenta at term
concepts.def_ours: Size and changes near birth; amnion and chorion fuse into the amniochorionic membrane.

concepts.name: Amniotic fluid
concepts.def_ours: Sources, volume, and fetal swallowing and urine in its turnover.

concepts.name: Polyhydramnios and oligohydramnios
concepts.def_ours: Too much fluid (e.g. can't swallow) or too little (e.g. kidneys absent).

concepts.name: Twins and their membranes
concepts.def_ours: Dizygotic twins come from two oocytes; monozygotic membranes depend on when one embryo splits.
concepts.misconception: All identical twins share one placenta.

concepts.name: Twin complications
concepts.def_ours: Conjoined twins and twin–twin transfusion.

concepts.name: Parturition (labour)
concepts.def_ours: Three stages: cervix opens, baby delivered, placenta delivered.

concepts.name: Types of birth defects
concepts.def_ours: Malformation, disruption, deformation, sequence, syndrome, association.

concepts.name: Principles of teratology
concepts.def_ours: Effect depends on genotype, timing, dose and mechanism; weeks 3–8 are most sensitive.
concepts.misconception: Weeks 1–2 are the most sensitive (exposure then usually is all-or-none).

concepts.name: Key teratogens
concepts.def_ours: Infections (rubella, CMV, Zika), drugs (thalidomide, isotretinoin, valproate, warfarin), alcohol, radiation, maternal diabetes.

concepts.name: Preventing birth defects
concepts.def_ours: Folic acid, iodine, good glucose control, avoiding known teratogens.

concepts.name: Prenatal screening
concepts.def_ours: Ultrasound, maternal serum markers (AFP, hCG) and cell-free fetal DNA.

concepts.name: Amniocentesis and chorionic villus sampling
concepts.def_ours: Sampling fluid or villi for chromosomes and genes; timing and risks.

concepts.name: Fetal therapy
concepts.def_ours: Treating the fetus: transfusion, medicines, surgery.

concepts.name: Two ways to make bone
concepts.def_ours: Intramembranous (straight from mesenchyme) vs endochondral (cartilage model first).

concepts.name: Neurocranium
concepts.def_ours: Flat bones of the vault (membranous) and the cartilaginous skull base.

concepts.name: Viscerocranium
concepts.def_ours: Face and jaw bones, mostly from the first two pharyngeal arches.

concepts.name: Sutures and fontanelles
concepts.def_ours: Fibrous joints and soft spots let the skull mould at birth and the brain grow.

concepts.name: Craniosynostosis and skull defects
concepts.def_ours: Early fusion of sutures changes head shape (e.g. scaphocephaly, brachycephaly).

concepts.name: Skeletal dysplasias
concepts.def_ours: Achondroplasia (FGFR3) and other growth-plate disorders; cranioschisis; microcephaly.

concepts.name: Vertebrae from sclerotomes
concepts.def_ours: Each vertebra forms from the lower half of one sclerotome and upper half of the next.
concepts.misconception: One somite makes one vertebra.

concepts.name: Intervertebral disc
concepts.def_ours: Nucleus pulposus from the notochord, annulus fibrosus from sclerotome.

concepts.name: Vertebral defects
concepts.def_ours: Spina bifida occulta, scoliosis from hemivertebrae, fused neck vertebrae.

concepts.name: Ribs and sternum
concepts.def_ours: Ribs grow from vertebral costal processes; the sternum from paired bands in the body wall.

concepts.name: Rib and sternum defects
concepts.def_ours: Cervical ribs, cleft sternum.

concepts.name: Where muscles come from
concepts.def_ours: Skeletal muscle from paraxial mesoderm; smooth and cardiac muscle mostly from splanchnic mesoderm.

concepts.name: Myoblasts fuse into fibres
concepts.def_ours: Myoblasts line up and fuse into multinucleated muscle fibres.

concepts.name: Primaxial domain and abaxial domain
concepts.def_ours: Muscles from cells staying near the somite vs cells crossing into lateral plate.

concepts.name: Epaxial and hypaxial muscles
concepts.def_ours: Back muscles (dorsal ramus) vs body-wall and limb muscles (ventral ramus).
concepts.misconception: Limb muscles are epaxial and supplied by dorsal rami.

concepts.name: Dermatomes and myotomes keep their nerve
concepts.def_ours: Each segment's skin and muscle stay with its spinal nerve, even after migrating.

concepts.name: Molecular regulation of muscle
concepts.def_ours: Neighbour signals switch on muscle genes such as MYOD.

concepts.name: Patterning of muscles
concepts.def_ours: Connective tissue sets the muscle pattern.

concepts.name: Head muscles
concepts.def_ours: From somitomeres and occipital somites: eye, tongue and pharyngeal-arch muscles.

concepts.name: Tendons
concepts.def_ours: Tendons form from a sclerotome region beside the myotome.

concepts.name: Limb muscles
concepts.def_ours: Cells migrate into limb buds and form dorsal (extensor) and ventral (flexor) masses.

concepts.name: Cardiac muscle
concepts.def_ours: From splanchnic mesoderm around the heart tube; some become conducting fibres.

concepts.name: Smooth muscle
concepts.def_ours: Gut-wall smooth muscle from splanchnic mesoderm; vessel smooth muscle from local mesoderm or crest.

concepts.name: Muscle defects
concepts.def_ours: Poland sequence, prune belly syndrome, muscular dystrophy.

concepts.name: Limb buds
concepts.def_ours: Arm buds appear around day 26–27 and leg buds a day or two later, from lateral plate mesoderm under ectoderm.

concepts.name: Shaping and rotating the limbs
concepts.def_ours: Hand and foot plates; apoptosis (cell death) frees the digits, then arms rotate laterally and legs medially.
concepts.misconception: Arms and legs rotate the same way.

concepts.name: Limb bone growth
concepts.def_ours: Cartilage models ossify from the shaft; growth plates lengthen bones until adulthood.

concepts.name: Apical ectodermal ridge
concepts.def_ours: A ridge at the bud tip releases FGFs that keep the limb growing outward.

concepts.name: Zone of polarizing activity
concepts.def_ours: A posterior patch makes SHH and sets thumb-to-little-finger order.

concepts.name: Limb musculature and innervation
concepts.def_ours: Nerves enter with muscle masses; limb dermatomes follow the rotation.

concepts.name: Limb defects
concepts.def_ours: Amelia, meromelia (e.g. thalidomide phocomelia), polydactyly, syndactyly, split hand.

concepts.name: Clubfoot and other limb anomalies
concepts.def_ours: Clubfoot, hip dysplasia, arthrogryposis, amniotic bands.

concepts.name: The heart works first
concepts.def_ours: The first organ to function; it begins beating at about day 22.

concepts.name: Primary heart field
concepts.def_ours: Splanchnic mesoderm cranial to the neural plate forms a crescent of heart precursors.

concepts.name: Secondary heart field
concepts.def_ours: Cells added later make the outflow tract, right ventricle and parts of the atria.

concepts.name: Heart tube forms
concepts.def_ours: Body folding brings two endocardial tubes together; they fuse into one tube in the pericardial cavity.

concepts.name: Parts of the heart tube
concepts.def_ours: Inflow (sinus venosus), atrium, ventricle and outflow (bulbus: conus and truncus).

concepts.name: Cardiac looping
concepts.def_ours: The tube bends to the right so the atria move up and back and the ventricle down and forward.

concepts.name: Dextrocardia and heterotaxy
concepts.def_ours: Leftward looping puts the heart on the right; often with other laterality defects.

concepts.name: Molecular regulation of the heart
concepts.def_ours: NKX2.5, TBX5 and BMP/WNT signals specify and pattern the heart.

concepts.name: Sinus venosus
concepts.def_ours: Blood return shifts right: the right horn forms the smooth atrial wall (edge: crista terminalis), the left the coronary sinus.

concepts.name: How septa form
concepts.def_ours: Endocardial cushions and growing ridges meet to divide the heart.

concepts.name: Atrial septation
concepts.def_ours: Septum primum, two ostia and septum secundum leave a flap valve: the foramen ovale.
concepts.misconception: The foramen ovale closes before birth.

concepts.name: Atrial septal defects
concepts.def_ours: Secundum defects, probe-patent foramen ovale, cushion defects.

concepts.name: AV canal and valves
concepts.def_ours: Cushions divide the AV canal and help form mitral and tricuspid valves.

concepts.name: Outflow tract septation
concepts.def_ours: Neural-crest ridges spiral and fuse, splitting the truncus into aorta and pulmonary trunk.

concepts.name: Ventricular septum
concepts.def_ours: A muscular part grows up; a membranous part closes the gap.

concepts.name: VSD, tetralogy, transposition, truncus
concepts.def_ours: Membranous VSD; outflow septum shifted (tetralogy) or not spiralling (transposition) or absent (persistent truncus).

concepts.name: Valve defects and hypoplastic left heart
concepts.def_ours: Stenoses, atresias, Ebstein anomaly (tricuspid displaced) and the hypoplastic left heart.

concepts.name: Conducting system
concepts.def_ours: Pacemaker in the sinus venosus region, then the AV node and bundle.

concepts.name: Pharyngeal arch arteries and their fates
concepts.def_ours: 3rd → carotids; 4th → aortic arch (left) and right subclavian; 6th → pulmonary arteries and ductus.
concepts.misconception: All six arches are present at the same time.

concepts.name: Recurrent laryngeal nerve asymmetry
concepts.def_ours: The left nerve hooks under the ductus; the right under the subclavian.

concepts.name: Vitelline and umbilical arteries
concepts.def_ours: Vitelline arteries → gut arteries; umbilical arteries → internal iliac branches and medial umbilical ligaments.

concepts.name: Vitelline, umbilical and cardinal veins
concepts.def_ours: Become the portal system, ductus venosus, SVC and IVC.

concepts.name: Arterial defects
concepts.def_ours: Patent ductus, coarctation, double aortic arch, aberrant right subclavian.

concepts.name: Fetal circulation
concepts.def_ours: Three shunts — ductus venosus, foramen ovale, ductus arteriosus — bypass liver and lungs.
concepts.misconception: The fetal lungs oxygenate the blood.

concepts.name: Changes at birth and adult remnants
concepts.def_ours: Shunts close and leave ligaments (ligamentum arteriosum, round ligament of the liver) and the fossa ovalis.

concepts.name: Lymphatic system
concepts.def_ours: Lymph sacs and ducts form beside the veins.

concepts.name: Respiratory diverticulum
concepts.def_ours: A ventral outpouching of the foregut; tracheoesophageal ridges fuse into the tracheoesophageal septum, separating it from the oesophagus.

concepts.name: Tracheoesophageal fistula and oesophageal atresia
concepts.def_ours: Faulty separation joins trachea and oesophagus; fluid can't be swallowed (polyhydramnios).

concepts.name: Larynx
concepts.def_ours: Endodermal lining; cartilages and muscles from arches 4 and 6 (vagus).

concepts.name: Bronchi and lung branching
concepts.def_ours: Buds branch into main, lobar and segmental bronchi; splanchnic mesoderm gives cartilage and muscle.

concepts.name: Lungs and pleura
concepts.def_ours: Lungs grow into the pericardioperitoneal canals, picking up visceral and parietal pleura.

concepts.name: Lung maturation phases
concepts.def_ours: Pseudoglandular, canalicular, terminal sac, then alveolar (continuing after birth).
concepts.misconception: All alveoli form before birth.

concepts.name: Surfactant and preterm breathing
concepts.def_ours: Type II alveolar cells make surfactant late in pregnancy; too little causes respiratory distress.

concepts.name: Lung anomalies
concepts.def_ours: Lung hypoplasia, ectopic lobes.

concepts.name: Gut divisions and their arteries
concepts.def_ours: Foregut–coeliac, midgut–superior mesenteric, hindgut–inferior mesenteric.

concepts.name: Molecular regionalisation of the gut
concepts.def_ours: Gradients and transcription factors give each gut region its identity.

concepts.name: Dorsal and ventral mesenteries
concepts.def_ours: The gut hangs from a dorsal mesentery; a ventral one exists only near the stomach and liver.

concepts.name: Oesophagus
concepts.def_ours: Lengthens as the heart and lungs descend.

concepts.name: Stomach rotation
concepts.def_ours: Rotates 90° clockwise on its long axis and tilts, so the left vagus ends up in front.

concepts.name: Omenta and lesser sac
concepts.def_ours: Greater omentum from dorsal mesogastrium; lesser sac behind the stomach, entered by the epiploic foramen; peritoneal ligaments link organs.

concepts.name: Duodenum
concepts.def_ours: From the end of the foregut and start of the midgut; forms a C-loop; its lumen fills then reopens (atresia or stenosis if not: 'double bubble').

concepts.name: Liver and gallbladder
concepts.def_ours: A liver bud grows into the septum transversum and forms the parenchyma; ventral mesentery forms the lesser omentum and falciform ligament.

concepts.name: Pyloric stenosis
concepts.def_ours: Thickened pyloric muscle causes forceful vomiting in young infants.

concepts.name: Spleen
concepts.def_ours: Forms from mesenchyme in the dorsal mesogastrium; accessory spleens are common.
concepts.misconception: The spleen is a gut (endoderm) organ.

concepts.name: Molecular regulation of liver induction
concepts.def_ours: Signals from heart and septum transversum turn foregut endoderm into liver.

concepts.name: Biliary atresia and duct anomalies
concepts.def_ours: Bile ducts fail to open or are doubled.

concepts.name: Pancreas
concepts.def_ours: Dorsal and ventral buds; the ventral bud swings behind and fuses; ducts join.

concepts.name: Annular pancreas and pancreas divisum
concepts.def_ours: A ring of pancreas around the duodenum, or ducts that fail to join.

concepts.name: Physiological umbilical herniation
concepts.def_ours: The fast-growing midgut loop bulges into the cord in weeks 6–10, then returns.
concepts.misconception: Physiological herniation is an omphalocele.

concepts.name: Midgut rotation
concepts.def_ours: The loop turns 270° counterclockwise around the superior mesenteric artery.

concepts.name: Fixation and retroperitoneal parts
concepts.def_ours: Some mesenteries fuse to the back wall, making parts secondarily retroperitoneal.

concepts.name: Midgut defects
concepts.def_ours: Malrotation and volvulus, Meckel diverticulum, vitelline remnants, atresia.

concepts.name: Cloaca division
concepts.def_ours: The urorectal septum splits the cloaca into rectum and urogenital sinus.

concepts.name: Anal canal: two origins
concepts.def_ours: Upper part from endoderm, lower from ectoderm; vessels, nerves and lymph differ at the pectinate line.

concepts.name: Hindgut defects
concepts.def_ours: Anorectal malformations and fistulas; Hirschsprung disease (missing crest ganglia).

concepts.name: Three kidney systems
concepts.def_ours: Pronephros, mesonephros and metanephros appear in sequence; only the metanephros stays.
concepts.misconception: All three systems form the adult kidney together.

concepts.name: Mesonephros and its duct
concepts.def_ours: A temporary kidney whose duct later forms male genital ducts.

concepts.name: Metanephros: two sources
concepts.def_ours: Ureteric bud → collecting system; metanephric blastema → nephrons; they induce each other.
concepts.misconception: Nephrons and collecting ducts come from the same tissue.

concepts.name: Nephron formation
concepts.def_ours: Renal vesicle → S-shaped tubule → Bowman capsule with glomerulus.

concepts.name: Kidney ascent
concepts.def_ours: Kidneys rise from the pelvis, taking new arteries; horseshoe or pelvic kidney if stuck.

concepts.name: Renal anomalies
concepts.def_ours: Agenesis (with Potter sequence), cystic kidneys, duplicated ureter.

concepts.name: Bladder and urethra
concepts.def_ours: From the urogenital sinus; trigone from mesonephric ducts; the urachus links to the allantois.

concepts.name: Urachal anomalies
concepts.def_ours: Urachal fistula, cyst or sinus at the navel.

concepts.name: Molecular regulation of kidney development
concepts.def_ours: WT1, GDNF and RET drive bud–blastema talk.

concepts.name: Wilms tumour
concepts.def_ours: A childhood kidney tumour from nephron precursors, linked to WT1.

concepts.name: Sex determination
concepts.def_ours: SRY on the Y makes a testis; ovary development needs its own genes (e.g. WNT4).
concepts.misconception: Female development needs no genes at all.

concepts.name: Indifferent gonad
concepts.def_ours: Genital ridges plus arriving germ cells form sex cords before sex shows.

concepts.name: Testis
concepts.def_ours: Medullary cords with Sertoli cells; Leydig cells make testosterone.

concepts.name: Ovary
concepts.def_ours: Cortical cords break into follicles around oogonia.

concepts.name: Genital ducts: two sets
concepts.def_ours: Testosterone keeps mesonephric ducts; AMH removes paramesonephric ducts; without them the reverse.
concepts.misconception: Testosterone makes the paramesonephric ducts regress.

concepts.name: Male ducts and glands
concepts.def_ours: Epididymis, ductus deferens, seminal vesicle; prostate from urethra.

concepts.name: Female ducts and vagina
concepts.def_ours: Tubes, uterus and upper vagina; vaginal plate canalises.

concepts.name: Uterine and vaginal anomalies
concepts.def_ours: Double uterus, bicornuate uterus, vaginal atresia.

concepts.name: External genitalia
concepts.def_ours: Genital tubercle, folds and swellings form either set; DHT makes the male form.

concepts.name: Hypospadias and epispadias
concepts.def_ours: Urethral opening on the underside or top of the penis.

concepts.name: Differences of sex development
concepts.def_ours: CAH, androgen insensitivity, 5α-reductase deficiency, ovotesticular DSD.

concepts.name: Descent of the testis
concepts.def_ours: The gubernaculum guides the testis through the inguinal canal, led by the processus vaginalis.

concepts.name: Inguinal hernia, hydrocele, cryptorchidism
concepts.def_ours: An open processus vaginalis or a testis that doesn't descend.

concepts.name: What builds the head and neck
concepts.def_ours: Pharyngeal arches, neural crest, paraxial mesoderm and placodes.

concepts.name: Pharyngeal arches
concepts.def_ours: Each arch has cartilage, muscle, a nerve and an artery.
concepts.misconception: Humans have gills or gill slits.

concepts.name: Arch derivatives
concepts.def_ours: 1 trigeminal, chewing, malleus/incus; 2 facial, expression, stapes; 3 glossopharyngeal; 4 and 6 vagus, larynx.

concepts.name: Stomodeum
concepts.def_ours: The primitive mouth, closed by the oropharyngeal membrane until it breaks.

concepts.name: Pharyngeal pouches
concepts.def_ours: 1 middle ear and tube; 2 tonsil; 3 thymus and inferior parathyroids; 4 superior parathyroids and C cells.
concepts.misconception: Inferior parathyroids come from pouch 4.

concepts.name: Pharyngeal clefts
concepts.def_ours: The first becomes the external ear canal; the rest are buried in the cervical sinus.

concepts.name: Arch and pouch defects
concepts.def_ours: Branchial cysts and fistulas, DiGeorge (22q11), first-arch syndromes.

concepts.name: Molecular regulation of facial development
concepts.def_ours: Crest cells carry patterning signals; first arch is Hox-free; SHH is needed.

concepts.name: Tongue
concepts.def_ours: Front two-thirds from arch 1, back third from arch 3 (and 4); muscles from occipital somites (XII). Touch V3 front, IX back; taste VII front.

concepts.name: Tongue-tie
concepts.def_ours: A short frenulum.

concepts.name: Thyroid descent
concepts.def_ours: Starts at the foramen cecum and descends in front of the gut via the thyroglossal duct.

concepts.name: Thyroglossal cyst and ectopic thyroid
concepts.def_ours: Leftover duct tissue forms a midline neck cyst; thyroid may stay at the tongue.

concepts.name: Face from five prominences
concepts.def_ours: Frontonasal, paired maxillary and mandibular prominences grow and merge.

concepts.name: Nasal placodes and prominences
concepts.def_ours: Placodes sink into pits ringed by medial and lateral nasal prominences.

concepts.name: Intermaxillary segment
concepts.def_ours: Merged medial nasal prominences form the philtrum, upper incisor area and primary palate.

concepts.name: Secondary palate
concepts.def_ours: Palatal shelves rise above the tongue and fuse; the incisive foramen marks the joint with the primary palate.

concepts.name: Cleft lip and cleft palate
concepts.def_ours: Clefts in front of the incisive foramen (lip, primary palate) vs behind (secondary palate).
concepts.misconception: Cleft lip and cleft palate are one defect.

concepts.name: Nasal cavities and sinuses
concepts.def_ours: Oronasal membrane breaks to make choanae; sinuses grow mostly after birth.

concepts.name: Teeth
concepts.def_ours: Dental lamina → bud, cap, bell; enamel from ectoderm, dentin and pulp from crest mesenchyme.

concepts.name: Tooth regulation and defects
concepts.def_ours: Signals that pattern teeth; tooth number and enamel defects.

concepts.name: Neural tube layers
concepts.def_ours: Ventricular (neuroepithelial), mantle (grey matter) and marginal (white matter) layers.

concepts.name: Alar and basal plates
concepts.def_ours: Dorsal alar plate = sensory; ventral basal plate = motor; the sulcus limitans divides them; the lateral horn (intermediate column) holds autonomic neurons.
concepts.misconception: The basal plate is sensory.

concepts.name: Spinal nerves and dorsal root ganglia
concepts.def_ours: Motor fibres leave from the basal plate; sensory neurons sit in crest-derived ganglia.

concepts.name: Myelination
concepts.def_ours: Schwann cells in nerves; oligodendrocytes in the cord and brain.

concepts.name: Position of the cord end
concepts.def_ours: The cord ends lower in the fetus and rises relative to the spine (about L3 at birth, higher in adults; exact adult level ⚑ X1 checks book vs anatomy sources).

concepts.name: Spina bifida types
concepts.def_ours: Occulta, meningocele, myelomeningocele, rachischisis; raised AFP; folic acid helps prevent.

concepts.name: Dorsoventral patterning of the tube
concepts.def_ours: SHH from notochord and floor plate makes ventral (motor) cells; BMPs from the roof make dorsal ones.

concepts.name: Brain vesicles and flexures
concepts.def_ours: Three primary vesicles become five; the tube bends at three flexures.

concepts.name: Hindbrain: medulla, pons, cerebellum
concepts.def_ours: Myelencephalon → medulla; metencephalon → pons and cerebellum.

concepts.name: Midbrain
concepts.def_ours: Colliculi and the narrow cerebral aqueduct.

concepts.name: Diencephalon and pituitary
concepts.def_ours: Thalamus and hypothalamus; pituitary: adenohypophysis (anterior lobe) from Rathke pouch; neurohypophysis (posterior lobe) from the infundibulum.
concepts.misconception: The whole pituitary comes from the brain.

concepts.name: Cerebral hemispheres
concepts.def_ours: Hemispheres, cortex, basal ganglia and commissures such as the corpus callosum.

concepts.name: Ventricles and CSF
concepts.def_ours: The tube's lumen becomes the ventricles; choroid plexuses make CSF.

concepts.name: Meninges
concepts.def_ours: Dura from mesoderm; pia and arachnoid largely from neural crest.

concepts.name: Brain defects
concepts.def_ours: Anencephaly, hydrocephalus, Chiari malformation, holoprosencephaly, microcephaly.

concepts.name: Brain patterning
concepts.def_ours: Rhombomeres with Hox codes, the isthmus organizer (FGF8) and forebrain SHH.

concepts.name: Cranial nerves
concepts.def_ours: Motor nuclei from basal plates; sensory ganglia from crest and placodes.

concepts.name: Sympathetic system
concepts.def_ours: Part of the autonomic nervous system: crest cells form chain ganglia; white and gray rami; splanchnic nerves.

concepts.name: Adrenal gland: two origins
concepts.def_ours: Cortex from mesoderm; medulla from neural crest.
concepts.misconception: The whole adrenal comes from one layer.

concepts.name: Parasympathetic system
concepts.def_ours: Brainstem and sacral outflow; ganglia from crest.

concepts.name: Neural crest tumours
concepts.def_ours: Pheochromocytoma and neuroblastoma arise from crest-derived adrenal medulla and ganglia.

concepts.name: Otic vesicle and inner ear
concepts.def_ours: Otic placode → vesicle → utricle (semicircular canals) and saccule (cochlea).

concepts.name: Membranous and bony labyrinth
concepts.def_ours: Mesenchyme around the membranous labyrinth becomes the bony capsule.

concepts.name: Middle ear
concepts.def_ours: Tympanic cavity and tube from pouch 1; ossicles from arches 1 and 2; the eardrum has all three layers.

concepts.name: External ear
concepts.def_ours: Canal from cleft 1; auricle from six hillocks; low-set ears flag syndromes.

concepts.name: Congenital hearing loss
concepts.def_ours: Genetic causes, rubella and other teratogens, ear malformations.

concepts.name: Optic cup and lens vesicle
concepts.def_ours: Optic vesicle from the forebrain becomes a cup; it induces the lens placode; the choroid fissure carries vessels.

concepts.name: Retina
concepts.def_ours: Inner cup wall → neural retina; outer wall → pigment layer.
concepts.misconception: Retinal detachment separates retina from choroid (it splits the two retinal layers).

concepts.name: Iris and ciliary body
concepts.def_ours: Cup rim plus mesenchyme; the iris muscles come from neuroectoderm.

concepts.name: Lens
concepts.def_ours: Lens fibres fill the vesicle.

concepts.name: Choroid, sclera and cornea
concepts.def_ours: Mesenchyme forms choroid and sclera, continuous with pia and dura; cornea in layers.

concepts.name: Vitreous and hyaloid artery
concepts.def_ours: Gel fills the cup; the hyaloid artery regresses except for the central retinal vessels.

concepts.name: Optic nerve
concepts.def_ours: Retinal axons travel through the optic stalk.

concepts.name: Molecular regulation of the eye
concepts.def_ours: PAX6 is the master gene; SHH splits one eye field into two.

concepts.name: Eye defects
concepts.def_ours: Coloboma, congenital cataract, microphthalmia, cyclopia.

concepts.name: Epidermis
concepts.def_ours: Layers from ectoderm; melanocytes from crest.

concepts.name: Dermis
concepts.def_ours: From dermatomes and lateral plate mesoderm.

concepts.name: Skin disorders
concepts.def_ours: Ichthyosis; pigment disorders (albinism, piebaldism) from melanocyte faults.

concepts.name: Hair
concepts.def_ours: Follicles grow down into the dermis; fine lanugo hair and vernix.

concepts.name: Nails
concepts.def_ours: Nail fields at digit tips.

concepts.name: Sweat glands
concepts.def_ours: Eccrine and apocrine glands grow down from the epidermis.

concepts.name: Mammary glands
concepts.def_ours: Along the mammary ridges; extra nipples along the line.

E.t.round-ligament-of-the-liver-ligament.term: Round ligament of the liver (ligamentum teres hepatis)
